page: Amazon Web Services c5d.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8275CL processor running at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz with x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). It is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3000 MHz, representing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core. The server contains no integrated GPUs.

A central differentiator of the c5d family is the inclusion of physical local instance storage. The c5d.2xlarge bundles a 200 GB local NVMe SSD directly attached to the host, bypassing network-attached storage latency. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps. Complementary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate mid-tier performance across general processing and memory subsystems. Geekbench 6 measures 1,172 in single-core and 4,511 in multi-core metrics, aligning with median results for its hardware tier. PassMark reports an overall CPU score of 8,429.69, accompanied by 7,256.7 in extended instruction sets and 2,854.81 in database operations. Memory bandwidth remains steady at 51.06 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 39.32 GB/sec for writes. However, certain execution profiles show constraints: stress-ng single-core computes (1,407.48), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.82 GB/sec), and Geekbench image processing (3,921.0) drop into lower quartiles. Machine learning inferences on 7B parameter models remain restricted (11.31 prompt tokens/sec and 6.57 generation tokens/sec) due to absence of hardware acceleration and moderate thread capacity.

The qualitative trade-off of the c5d.2xlarge centers on local I/O density against memory headroom. The local NVMe SSD offers high throughput and low-latency storage for caching, scratch space, and ephemeral logs without incurring external storage network delays. Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration and mid-range multi-core processing throughput, the instance is appropriate for batch computing, CI/CD compilation, distributed build pipelines, intermediate ETL processing, and web serving clusters requiring high-speed local disk caches.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 4-core, 8-vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8275CL processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a dedicated 200 GB local NVMe SSD, offering low-latency scratch storage. Network throughput features a 2 Gbps baseline, and no GPUs are included. Performance benchmarks exhibit balanced middle-tier results, such as a PassMark CPU score of 8,429.69 and multi-core Geekbench score of 4,511, though single-core compute and intensive compression tasks perform in lower tiers. The local NVMe drive paired with a 1:2 core-to-memory profile makes the c5d.2xlarge suited for CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, distributed compilation, and web serving workloads utilizing ephemeral caching.
